column1: # Golden vectors for SRS 5.11's FR-1207 and FR-1209 - the contacts analogue of
# metadata/hash_vectors.tsv, and it exists for the same reason.
# THIS FILE IS A CROSS-CLIENT CONFORMANCE SUITE. Prose will not hold two codebases
# byte-identical; a digest will. A client deriving a different source_hash cannot see
# what another client wrote (FR-1208); one deriving a different identity key would
# offer to update the wrong person (FR-1231).
# Pure ASCII on purpose, so no editor can normalise a case away. In the payload column
# \n stands for a newline and \r for a carriage return; both must be
# expanded before hashing. Writing this file caught an em dash in its own header, which
# is the constraint working.
# The dotted/undotted pair is deliberate and MUST hash differently: dot-stripping is
# right for one provider and wrong for every mail server that treats dots as
# significant, where applying it merges two colleagues into one contact.
# An empty identity_key is a real answer and not a gap: a card with no email has no
# automatic identity and is always written as a new contact.
# name
plain_vcard
crlf_vcard
folded_adr
mecard
no_email
upper_email
dotted
undotted
